edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $250,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholding. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit plans, subject to their terms.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Company shall pay the Executive six months of base salary at the rate in effect immediately before termination, in substantially equal installments through regular payroll. Severance is conditioned on the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of employment-related claims, provided that the release excludes claims for vested benefits, indemnification, enforcement of this Agreement, and rights that cannot lawfully be waived. The Company shall provide the release within seven days after termination. Payments shall commence on the first regular payroll date after the release becomes effective, with a catch-up payment for installments otherwise due, subject to applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. If the release consideration and revocation period spans two calendar years, payments shall commence in the second year. 'Cause' means only (a) conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty; (b) willful misconduct causing material harm to the Company; or (c) a willful, material breach of this Agreement. For any curable conduct under (b) or (c), Cause requires written notice specifying the conduct and at least 30 days to cure. Good-faith business judgments, ordinary negligence, and failure to meet performance targets do not constitute Cause.
edits.name: Severance and Cause

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY; INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY; LIMITED NON-SOLICITATION. No non-compete restriction shall apply. The Executive shall protect the Company’s nonpublic confidential information and use it only in performing duties for the Company. This obligation excludes information that becomes public without breach, is lawfully obtained without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of Company confidential information. Nothing prohibits legally protected disclosures, reporting possible violations to governmental authorities, cooperating with investigations, or making disclosures protected by applicable whistleblower law, including the trade-secret immunity provisions of 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b). The Executive assigns to the Company intellectual property created within the scope of employment or using Company confidential information, excluding pre-existing intellectual property and inventions excluded from assignment by applicable law. For six months following termination, and only to the extent permitted by applicable law, the Executive shall not directly and intentionally solicit for recruitment a Company employee with whom the Executive worked materially during the preceding 12 months, or solicit a customer with whom the Executive had material business contact during that period to terminate or materially reduce its business with the Company. General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring without prohibited solicitation are excluded. These restrictions do not prohibit employment by a competitor.
edits.name: Protective Covenants
